includedSites.name: Rosenborg Castle
includedSites.scope: The castle building and visitor-accessible historic interiors, halls, rooms, tower rooms, and the Treasury beneath the castle.

includedCollectionGroups.name: Historic royal interiors and objects
includedCollectionGroups.scope: The furnished rooms and halls associated with the Danish kings who resided at Rosenborg, together with the royal art treasures and objects displayed in the castle.

includedCollectionGroups.name: Danish crown jewels
includedCollectionGroups.scope: The crown-jewel sets displayed in the Treasury, including the Emerald Set, Rose-Cut Diamond Set, Brilliant-Cut Diamond Set, and Pearl-Ruby Set.

includedCollectionGroups.name: Royal crowns and Crown regalia
includedCollectionGroups.scope: The royal crowns and regalia presented in the Treasury, including objects with a documented connection to the Danish monarchy.

includedCollectionGroups.name: Historical clothing and other royal objects
includedCollectionGroups.scope: The historical clothing and other objects associated with the Rosenborg collection where they are presented at this site; current display and project status require downstream verification.

collectionBoundaries.boundaryRationale: Rosenborg is treated as one museum site and one editorial route: the castle, its preserved interiors, and its Treasury. The wider Royal Danish Collection is an institution with several separate castles and palaces, so institution-wide holdings are not merged into this scope.

uncertainties: The official site describes an ongoing Kingdom's Treasury project and a planned exhibition space for historical clothing and other objects; the exact objects and galleries visible on a given visit require downstream current-display verification.

The scope identifies official collection groups rather than enumerating every object or formal curatorial department; individual object identities and candidate-pool boundaries require later official object-page research.
